messages:
oncall-bot: INCIDENT ALERT: High container restart rate on gpu-serving-prod-7 (prefill OOM). 50 restarts in last 10m. Pager triggered for priority P1.

oncall-bot: Symptoms: CUDA OOM in prefill path, container restarted, latency spike to 5–7s for affected requests. Affected model: redwood-gpt-large-ctx.

alex_m: seeing the same in logs. repro rate ~0.6% but concentrated on long-context requests (>120k tokens).

sam_infra: attaching tail of recent pod logs:
```
2026-03-15T01:12:33Z ERROR runtime: CUDA error: out of memory while allocating 384MB
2026-03-15T01:12:33Z WARN runtime: prefill sequence length=132000, kv_cache_size=~1.1GB
2026-03-15T01:12:34Z INFO kubelet: container restart count=51
```

priya_ops: @alex_m @sam_infra I'll take pager handoff in 5. Priya oncall - standing by. Who's owning customer comms?

emma_support: I'll draft a short customer-facing blurb: "We are investigating intermittent failures affecting generation of very large-context requests. Impact limited to a small subset of requests with unusually long prompts — standard usage unaffected." Want to confirm before sending.

alex_m: thumbs up for that blurb. Quick mitigation: can we gate prefill path to reject >100k tokens temporarily? That would avoid OOM while we patch.

rick_eng: Agree. Two fast ones: 1) reject/trim prefill >100k at ingress (rate-limit & reply 413 or auto-trim with warning), 2) fallback to smaller model variant with lower kv cache for oversized requests. Both are config flips.

sam_infra: I can push an ingress rule now. Proposed nginx lua snippet to trim token count:
```
-- pseudo
if request.tokens > 100000 then
  request.tokens = 100000
  -- add header X-Prefill-Trimmed: true
end
```
Pushing to staging first.

priya_ops: please push and then we can promote to prod. @infra-bot can you queue a quick canary rollout to 3 pods?

infra-bot: Canary rollout scheduled to gpu-serving-prod-7 subset (3 pods). Rollout plan: update ingress rule -> wait 60s -> monitor restarts.

sam_infra: rolling to staging now. linking grafana panels: https://grafana.internal/gpu-serving/restarts and https://grafana.internal/latency/prefill.

alex_m: also seeing a few CUDA kernel launch failures in older drivers. Are those nodes on the same driver revision?

sam_infra: checking node metadata: gpu-serving-prod-7 nodes running driver 525.85.05, kernel build 5.15. Looks consistent. The main signal is token size -> kv cache blowup.

priya_ops: can we also reduce per-pod concurrent prefill workers from 4 -> 2 as temporary backpressure? That should reduce memory pressure.

rick_eng: good idea. Add to the runtime config: `max_prefill_workers: 2` and `prefill_token_cap: 100000`. I'll open a quick PR (link placeholder).

emma_support: Draft for customers updated: "Temporary mitigation applied: extremely large requests may be trimmed or rejected while we roll out fixes. We do not expect impact to normal traffic. We'll update in 2h or sooner." Approve?

alex_m: approve. Send once we confirm ingress rule on prod.

sam_infra: staging succeeded. Rollout to prod canary started.

infra-bot: Canary update: ingress rule updated on 3 pods. Monitoring restart counts.

(2m pass)

sam_infra: initial results: restart count stabilized on canary pods (0 restarts in 2m), latency for trimmed requests is back to normal but we are rejecting ~0.05% of requests due to token cap.

priya_ops: promote to 50% of serving fleet. @alex_m please be ready to revert if we see issues.

alex_m: ready. also adding temporary alert mute for noisy restart alerts for the controlled rollout window.

infra-bot: Promotion to 50% scheduled.

(20m pass)

sam_infra: prod 50% rollout done. Restart spike not observed across fleet. Overall restart rate dropped from ~48/10m -> 2/10m.

rick_eng: pushing follow-up: we should implement a proper soft-trim with deterministic summary before prefill (truncate and append "... [trimmed]"), plus an evaluation job to check quality impact. I'll own the PR.

priya_ops: customer comms ready. Sending now.

emma_support: Customer update sent to impacted accounts (list attached). No major escalations so far.

alex_m: root cause hypothesis: very long-context requests created kv cache allocations that exceeded per-GPU memory accounting and triggered OOM during prefill phase. Mitigation worked by trimming/preventing extreme prefill sizes and lowering concurrency.

sam_infra: logs showing final stabilisation:
```
2026-03-15T01:48:16Z INFO runtime: prefill tokens=98732, trimmed=true, user_id=acct-12345
2026-03-15T01:48:17Z INFO kubelet: container restart count=2
```

priya_ops: Postmortem owners and next steps:
- Immediate (oncall): monitor for 24h, keep token cap at 100k until PR merged. (owner: sam_infra)
- Short term (1 week): implement soft-trim + fallback routing to small model + eval (owner: rick_eng)
- Medium (2–4 weeks): KV cache per-request accounting + graceful OOM mitigation in runtime (owner: alex_m)
- Customer comms (support): targeted outreach and follow-up with ops runbook (owner: emma_support)

emma_support: adding action item: create canned reply for support about "large prompt" failures and checklist to advise customers to chunk or lower context size.

alex_m: I'll schedule a post-incident review tomorrow 10:00 UTC. Please add logs and sample request payloads to the incident doc.

priya_ops: thanks all. Handoff to night oncall in 15. Full incident channel status: mitigated, monitoring.

oncall-bot: Handoff complete. Next oncall: priya_ops.

(END)
